events/albanian-autocephaly-1922/title: Congress of Berat proclaims Albanian Orthodox autocephaly
events/albanian-autocephaly-1922/summary: Albanian Orthodox delegates meeting at Berat in September 1922 proclaimed an autocephalous church using the Albanian language, a movement associated with Fan Noli, who had founded Albanian Orthodox parishes in the United States from 1908. Constantinople recognised the autocephaly in 1937.
events/albanian-autocephaly-1922/causes/: Albanian independence (1912) and national language movement
Desire for Albanian-language liturgy instead of Greek
events/albanian-autocephaly-1922/consequ: Church suppressed when Albania declared itself an atheist state (1967)
events/polish-autocephaly-1924/title: Tomos of autocephaly for the Polish Orthodox Church
events/polish-autocephaly-1924/summary: With most of its faithful Belarusian and Ukrainian inhabitants of the restored Polish state, the Orthodox Church in Poland received a Tomos of autocephaly from Constantinople in November 1924. The Moscow Patriarchate did not accept it, and granted its own act of autocephaly in 1948 after Poland entered the Soviet sphere.
events/polish-autocephaly-1924/causes/1: Polish government's wish to sever the church from Moscow
events/polish-autocephaly-1924/causes/2: Collapse of the pre-revolutionary Russian church order
events/polish-autocephaly-1924/consequen: Rival canonical narratives (1924 vs 1948) about the source of autocephaly
Precedent later cited in the Ukrainian dispute
events/scopes-trial-1925/summary: Teacher John Scopes was tried for teaching evolution contrary to Tennessee's Butler Act; William Jennings Bryan helped the prosecution and Clarence Darrow the defence. Scopes was convicted (later overturned on a technicality), but press coverage portrayed fundamentalists as backward, accelerating their withdrawal from mainline institutions.
events/united-church-of-canada-1925/titl: Inauguration of the United Church of Canada
events/united-church-of-canada-1925/summ: On 10 June 1925 at the Mutual Street Arena in Toronto, the Methodist Church (Canada), the Congregational Union of Canada, about two-thirds of the Presbyterian Church in Canada and the local union churches of the West united as the United Church of Canada. A third of Presbyterians, voting against union, continued the Presbyterian Church in Canada.
events/united-church-of-canada-1925/caus: Prairie settlements unable to support competing denominations
Two decades of negotiation (Basis of Union, 1908)
events/united-church-of-canada-1925/cons: Lasting legal and pastoral bitterness with continuing Presbyterians
Later formal apologies for its role in residential schools (1986, 1998)
events/cristero-war-1926/summary: Enforcement of the anticlerical articles of Mexico's 1917 constitution by President Calles led bishops to suspend public worship and Catholic peasants to rise up with the cry '¡Viva Cristo Rey!'. Around 90,000 died before a 1929 settlement; many martyrs, including the Jesuit Miguel Pro, were later beatified or canonised.
events/lambeth-conference-1930/summary: Resolution 15 of the Lambeth Conference becomes the first official church statement to accept contraception: where there is a morally sound reason to limit or avoid parenthood and abstinence is not suitable, other methods may be used in the light of Christian principles. Pius XI’s Casti Connubii (December 1930) reaffirms Catholic prohibition.
events/lambeth-conference-1930/consequen: Most Protestant churches accept contraception by the 1960s
events/aladura-revival-1930/summary: Joseph Ayo Babalola, a former road-roller driver, led a healing revival at Oke-Oye, Ilesa in 1930 that drew vast crowds. The Yoruba 'praying' (aladura) churches — Christ Apostolic Church, Cherubim and Seraphim, Church of the Lord (Aladura) — combined prayer, prophecy and healing with African forms.
events/aladura-revival-1930/causes/1: Dissatisfaction with mission churches' approach to healing
events/syro-malankara-reunion-1930/summa: On 20 September 1930 Archbishop Geevarghese Mar Ivanios, founder of the Bethany monastic movement, and Bishop Jacob Mar Theophilos of the Malankara Orthodox church were received into communion with Rome while keeping the West Syriac liturgy, creating the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church.
events/syro-malankara-reunion-1930/cause: Ecumenical overtures from Rome on condition of retaining the Antiochene rite
events/barth-brunner-debate-1934/summary: In 1934 Emil Brunner’s Nature and Grace argued for a “point of contact” and limited natural revelation; Karl Barth replied with Nein! (No!), rejecting all natural theology as the opening through which the “German Christians” had brought race and nation into the church.
events/barth-brunner-debate-1934/consequ: Made rejection of natural theology a hallmark of Barthian theology
Shaped Protestant debate on general revelation for decades
events/barmen-declaration-1934/summary: At a synod in Barmen, Lutheran, Reformed and United delegates of the Confessing Church adopted six theses, largely drafted by Karl Barth, rejecting the pro-Nazi 'German Christians': Jesus Christ is the one Word of God whom we must trust and obey. It did not explicitly mention the Jews, a silence later lamented.
events/barmen-declaration-1934/causes/0: Nazi attempt to control the Protestant church
events/barmen-declaration-1934/consequen: Model of confessional resistance (e.g., Kairos, Belhar)
events/tambaram-conference-1938/summary: The International Missionary Council met at Madras Christian College, Tambaram, with for the first time a majority of delegates from the 'younger churches' of Asia, Africa and Latin America. Hendrik Kraemer's book on the Christian message in a non-Christian world framed debate on religions.
events/bultmann-demythologizing-1941/sum: In a 1941 lecture to the Confessing Church’s Society for Protestant Theology, Rudolf Bultmann argued that the New Testament’s mythological world-picture of heaven, hell, spirits and demons must be existentially interpreted, sparking a two-decade debate.
events/bultmann-demythologizing-1941/con: Demythologising became central to mid-20th-century theology
Prompted conservative and Barthian responses insisting on the reality of the powers
events/the-holocaust-1941/summary: The Nazi regime’s systematic murder of about six million Jews, along with Roma, disabled people and others. Its scale, and the complicity or silence of many baptised Christians, forced a profound rethinking of theodicy, providence, anti-Judaism and the churches’ relation to the state.
events/the-holocaust-1941/causes/0: Racial antisemitism, building on centuries of Christian anti-Judaism
events/the-holocaust-1941/consequences/0: Post-Holocaust theologies of protest, divine suffering and Jewish–Christian reconciliation
events/the-holocaust-1941/consequences/1: Nostra Aetate (1965) and Protestant repudiations of anti-Judaism
events/kyodan-formed-1941/title: Formation of the United Church of Christ in Japan (Kyodan)
events/kyodan-formed-1941/summary: In June 1941, under the Religious Organizations Law of 1939, some thirty Protestant denominations in Japan were brought into a single body, the Nihon Kirisuto Kyodan. Union was long desired by some Japanese Christians but was carried out under heavy state pressure in wartime.
events/kyodan-formed-1941/causes/0: Religious Organizations Law (1939) requiring registration of large bodies
events/kyodan-formed-1941/causes/1: Wartime nationalism and suspicion of foreign-linked churches
events/kyodan-formed-1941/consequences/0: After 1945 Anglicans, Lutherans, some Baptists, Holiness and Reformed groups withdrew
events/kyodan-formed-1941/consequences/1: 1967 'Confession on the Responsibility of the Kyodan During World War II' acknowledging complicity in the war
events/church-of-south-india-1947/summar: Anglicans, Methodists and the South India United Church (Presbyterian and Congregational) united on 27 September 1947, weeks after Indian independence, accepting episcopacy while recognising existing ministries. It was the first union of episcopal and non-episcopal churches.
events/church-of-south-india-1947/causes: Indian church leaders' desire for unity beyond Western divisions
events/church-of-south-india-1947/conseq: Model for Church of North India (1970) and other unions
events/world-council-of-churches-1948/su: Some 147 churches met in Amsterdam to form the WCC, uniting the Faith and Order and Life and Work movements. Most Orthodox churches joined by 1961; the Catholic Church is not a member but cooperates. Many evangelicals and Pentecostals remained critical of its theology and social activism.
events/feeney-letter-1949/title: Holy Office letter on the Feeney case
events/feeney-letter-1949/summary: The Holy Office’s letter to Archbishop Richard Cushing of Boston rejects Leonard Feeney’s strict interpretation of "outside the Church there is no salvation", teaching that those invincibly ignorant of the Church may be saved by implicit desire informed by perfect charity.
events/humani-generis-1950/title: Humani Generis permits study of evolution
events/humani-generis-1950/summary: In the encyclical Humani Generis (12 August 1950) Pius XII allowed Catholic scholars to investigate the evolution of the human body, provided they held that each soul is immediately created by God and did not embrace polygenism.
events/humani-generis-1950/consequences/: Opened official Catholic space for evolutionary creation
John Paul II (1996) called evolution “more than a hypothesis”
events/assumption-dogma-1950/title: Dogma of the Assumption of Mary
events/assumption-dogma-1950/summary: In Munificentissimus Deus (1 November 1950) Pius XII defined that Mary, having completed the course of her earthly life, was assumed body and soul into heavenly glory — the only universally recognised ex cathedra definition after 1870. Orthodox believe in her Dormition and bodily assumption but reject the papal definition; Protestants mostly reject the doctrine as unbiblical.
events/willingen-conference-1952/summary: Meeting of the International Missionary Council at Willingen, Germany, which grounded mission in the sending activity of the triune God; the term missio Dei, popularised soon afterwards by Karl Hartenstein, became the central concept of 20th-century ecumenical missiology.
events/willingen-conference-1952/consequ: Integration of the IMC into the WCC (1961)
events/three-self-patriotic-movement-195: After the 1950 'Christian Manifesto' and expulsion of foreign missionaries, China's Protestants were organised under the state-sanctioned Three-Self (self-governing, self-supporting, self-propagating) Patriotic Movement. Christians refusing registration, such as Wang Mingdao and Watchman Nee's Little Flock, were imprisoned; unregistered 'house churches' grew.
events/united-church-of-christ-1957/titl: Uniting General Synod forms the United Church of Christ
events/united-church-of-christ-1957/summ: On 25 June 1957 in Cleveland, the Evangelical and Reformed Church (a 1934 union of German Reformed and Evangelical Synod churches) and the General Council of the Congregational Christian Churches united as the United Church of Christ. A Statement of Faith followed in 1959.
events/united-church-of-christ-1957/caus: Ecumenical hopes for American Protestant unity
Mainline cooperation after the Second World War
events/united-church-of-christ-1957/cons: Some Congregational churches stayed out, forming the National Association of Congregational Christian Churches (1955) and the Conservative Congregational Christian Conference
Joined the Formula of Agreement (1997) with Lutherans, Presbyterians and Reformed
